messages:
maria_sales: Hey team — ArdentPay wants final run plan for the POC. They care about 99th pct latency under 450ms at sustained 150 qps, and short microbursts to 500 qps for up to 45s. Also asking for an indicative monthly cost for Dedicated with burst.

devin_se: Draft load profile below. Want to confirm: interactive chat workload (avg prompt 120 tokens, response 250 tokens). We planned a 30m soak at 150 qps then 3 x 1m microbursts to 500 qps, plus a 5m steady ramp. Does that match their test spec?

maria_sales: Yes — that matches. They also asked about encryption-at-rest and HSM for keys (legal requirement). Ellie can you confirm feasibility and any impact on latency?

ellie_security: HSM/KMS is fine for Dedicated and Private. With HSM there is a small crypto latency on key unwrap (single-digit ms on our side) — negligible vs token gen. We need a signed ATO addendum and proof of KMS integration; ops will need to enable CMEK in the provisioned cluster.

kai_perf: For the benchmark: recommend model variant rdx-large-quant (verified in our catalog) with KV-prefix caching enabled and per-tenant cache hotkey TTL 10m. Use batch window 10ms, dynamic batching up to 64 tokens/batch. Expected throughput per GPU: ~320 qps sustained for this workload. For 150 qps sustained we'll need 1 reserved node + autoscale headroom for bursts.

sam_eng: Quick cost ballpark (very rough): Dedicated reserved node (r4.x8g) estimated $9,200/mo; add 1 burst node on demand max ~+$1,100/mo amortized if used occasionally. If they want strict SLA for bursts we recommend 2 reserved + burst buffer (adds ~$9k). I can produce a more precise SKU by region.

devin_se: Test config (k6-like) below — will run from our east-us load agents:

```
scenarios:
  chat_sustain:
    executor: constant-arrival-rate
    rate: 150
    duration: 30m
    payload: {prompt_size:120, response_size:250}
  microburst:
    executor: constant-arrival-rate
    rate: 500
    duration: 1m
    pause: 5m
    repeat: 3
headers:
  Authorization: "Bearer <POC_KEY>"
  X-Model: "rdx-large-quant"
  X-Prefer-Cache: "kv-prefix"
```

kai_perf: Add tracing headers so we can capture tail latencies per-token: `X-Trace-Id` and enable sampling at 100% for the run. Also configure request histogram export to the console (rollup by route).

opsbot: [runbot] scheduled benchmark job id=bench-7401 started on agent-east-3. Tests will upload results to /bench-results/ardentpay/7401234567.json

devin_se: Small gotcha — cold-starts for quant models when cache empty can add ~80–120ms on first tokens. We should prewarm with a 2m 20qps cold-sweep to warm kernel paths and KV cache.

maria_sales: Good call. Add prewarm. Can someone write the short blurb I can send to procurement about encryption and isolation? They want bullet points for contract.

ellie_security: Draft bullets: "Dedicated capacity with tenant isolation; CMEK-backed secrets via your KMS/HSM; VPC peering/private link available; Audit logs retained X days; SOC2 + ISO27001 controls in place; deployment certificate for on-prem options." Use that and I can add legal wording.

sam_eng: I'll run cost calc for east-us and eu-west and post numbers by EOD. Also note: if they want guaranteed 500 qps bursts for 45s, we should recommend pre-reserving burst capacity (dedicated burst nodes) otherwise autoscale cold spin-up could add 200–400ms during ramp.

maria_sales: API key for the POC is ready. Devin — can you kick off the prewarm and the soak today? We'll coordinate with ArdentPay for the test window at 15:00 UTC.

devin_se: On it. Starting prewarm now. I'll paste a short summary + link to results when done.

opsbot: [runbot] prewarm complete. summary: 2m @20qps, average latency 82ms, cold-start median 110ms.

kai_perf: Nice. After soak I'll run a quick tail analysis and flag any >450ms 99p events with associated request traces.

maria_sales: Thanks all. Once Devin posts the results I'll send the exec summary + Sam's cost table to procurement and schedule legal review for HSM addendum. :thumbsup:

devin_se: Results uploaded: /bench-results/ardentpay/7401234567.json — quick highlights: soak 30m sustained 150 qps, 99p = 392ms; microburst peaks handled, P95 ~220ms, cold-start blips seen on first 10 requests only. Full CSV attached in the result folder.

maria_sales: This is great. Can you also include the specific fallback plan if load exceeds capacity (e.g., degrade to rdx-medium or route to another region)? They asked about graceful degradation.

kai_perf: Fallback options: 1) route to rdx-medium (cheaper, slightly higher latency), 2) degrade sampling rate for non-critical telemetry, 3) enable best-effort batching to reduce cost. I'll write a one-paragraph fallback policy.

maria_sales: Perfect — putting this in the POC report. We'll ask for procurement to confirm HSM timeline and sign the addendum. Closing loop after legal OK.

ellie_security: FYI addendum template attached here: /security-templates/hsm-addendum-v2.pdf

maria_sales: Thanks team — really helpful. I'll loop back after procurement responds.
